name: Hedged requests (cutting tail latency)
description: Four API servers. From second 20, instance 1 becomes 6× slower (not broken enough to fail, only slow). The load balancer still gives it a quarter of the requests: without hedging, p99 jumps from 84 ms to 218 ms. This connection uses hedged requests: when a read has no reply after 40 ms, a second copy goes to another instance, and the first success counts. p99 drops to 114 ms, at the cost of about 15% more calls; the losing copy still runs to the end downstream. Only reads are hedged, because sending a write twice is not safe. Set "Hedged request" to 0 to compare.
